# Job cards: numbering, status, invoicing, notes and assignees

> Detail split out of CLAUDE.md. Read before touching job numbering, job status, invoicing/archiving, deletion, comments or who is assigned.

## Numbering

**Job card auto-numbering**: Job numbers are auto-generated from two settings: `job_number_prefix` (e.g. `"DH-"`) and `job_number_next` (e.g. `"00001"`). The format preserves leading zeros (width of `job_number_next` string). On each job card creation, the server generates `{prefix}{paddedNumber}`, validates uniqueness, inserts the record, then increments `job_number_next`. Deleted job numbers are never reused. Numbers are compared without regard to case (Windows folders are case-insensitive, so `dh-0001` would share `DH-0001`'s folder); stored values keep the case typed. The prefix rule (letters, digits, `-`, `_`, up to 10) is judged only when the prefix actually changes, so a prefix saved before the rule existed does not block saving the other job-number settings. Settings refuses a starting number at or below the highest number actually handed out — the existing jobs plus deleted ones (read from the delete entries in the trail). The counter's own current value is not a floor, so a mistyped jump (e.g. 50000 for 00500) can be set back down. The job number field is read-only in the create form. Admin configures prefix and starting number in Settings > Job Card Numbering. If not configured, job card creation is blocked with an error message.

## Work-driven automatic status

**Work-driven automatic status**: A job's status follows the shop floor — it is recomputed from logged work on every work event (timer start/stop, time block added or deleted, finished quantity edited, and — since 2026-09-25 — a part added, changed or removed via `jobcard-items.js`, since a line change also changes what completion needs) by `syncStatusToWork` in `server/src/utils/jobStatusAuto.js`. Rule: every line at (or over) its ordered quantity ⇒ `DONE`; otherwise ⇒ `IN_PROGRESS`. Completion sums the good pieces (`qty`) from **finished** time blocks per line and compares to the line's quantity; a job with no lines, or any line whose quantity is missing/zero, is never complete. **A job with no logged work at all is left alone** — there's no shop-floor reality yet for its status to follow, so it stays whatever people set it to (Quote, Open, Awaiting Material, …); this is also why a part being added, changed or removed before any work starts never nudges the status. The one exception is **deleting a job's last time block**: that is a work event, and the status it leaves (often `DONE`) came from the deleted work, so the delete route passes `workRemoved` and the job is recomputed as usual — back to `IN_PROGRESS` rather than claiming Done with nothing logged. This **overrides** a manual status flip once work exists: if a manager moves a job elsewhere and a worker then logs work, it snaps back to match reality — to hold a finished job in another state the work itself must change. The only status it never touches is `INVOICED` (terminal); it also no-ops on archived jobs and when the status already matches. It does **not** write its own history row — it returns the `{ from, to }` change (or null) and the calling work route folds it into the history entry it already writes for that work event, so one action shows as one audit row carrying both the work change and the status move. Auto-status failures never break the work action. This is why **quantity is now required and must be a positive whole number** on every line item — it is the completion target. Enforced client-side (`jobCardValidation.mjs`, number input in `ItemsTab.jsx`) and server-side (`validateItemQuantities` in `itemValidation.js`) on create and update. **Every part route's reply carries `jobStatus` only when that write actually moved the status** — `jobcard-items.js`'s add/update/delete each fold `syncStatusToWork`'s result into `jobStatus` only when non-null, so a slow reply can never re-assert a status the user has since picked themselves, the same way the time routes already let a status move surface without a separate re-fetch.

## Who can set status manually

**Non-management (worker) status changes are narrow.** A worker may only move a job **to** `IN_PROGRESS` or `AWAITING_MATERIAL`, and only **from** `OPEN`, `IN_PROGRESS` or `AWAITING_MATERIAL` — everything else (any other target status, or moving away from any other current status such as `DONE`, `CUST_NOTIFIED`, `QUOTE` or `INVOICED`) is management-only and refused with 403 `{ error: 'Only management can set that status' }`. A no-op (setting a job to the status it's already at) is always allowed, for any role. The reasoning: `IN_PROGRESS` and `DONE` are normally driven by logged work (see above) and management owns every office-side status decision — the one manual nudge a worker genuinely needs is flagging "waiting on material" and clearing it again. The rule itself — `canSetStatus(canManage, fromStatus, toStatus)`, plus `canChangeStatus`, `settableStatusValues` and `offeredStatusValues` (the "only management is offered Invoiced" picker filter) — lives once in `server/src/shared/jobStatus.js`, built from the worker-settable/worker-from lists in the one shared data file, `server/src/shared/jobStatuses.json` (in the server folder so the packaged app, which copies the whole server folder, carries it); the server reads it directly and the client imports it at build time (the job list's status column and the job screen's status picker import `canChangeStatus`/`offeredStatusValues` straight from it), so the two can no longer drift apart by hand. `server/src/middleware/auth.js`'s own `canSetStatus(role, fromStatus, toStatus)` is a thin role-to-boolean wrapper around the shared function — the role check (`isManagement`) is the only thing that stays there. Only `PATCH /jobcards/:id/status` actually calls it: that route is reachable by any role and checks it after loading the existing job, before any write. `PUT /jobcards/:id` is management-only end to end (`requireManagement`), so it never runs a non-management request through this rule at all — a `canSetStatus` call there would always evaluate true (management may set any status) and was removed as dead code rather than kept as a no-op check. This subsumes the old INVOICED-only check (INVOICED was never worker-settable, so a worker still can't set it).

**Picking the status a job already has is not a change.** `PATCH /jobcards/:id/status` with the job's current status (a list or screen showing an older status — a timer started on another PC moves it) writes nothing, stamps no "Last Edited" and records no `from === to` trail entry; it answers with the job as it stands.

**"Last Edited" follows every edit, including the one-at-a-time ones.** Parts added/changed/removed (`jobcard-items.js`) and workers put on or taken off by management (`PUT`/`DELETE /jobcards/:id/assignees/:userId`) stamp `updated_by`/`updated_at` through `jobcardQueries.touch`, in the same transaction as the write, and only when something actually changed. Comments, files, prints and a worker's own self-assign do not count as edits of the job card and leave it alone.

## Invoicing and archiving

**Auto-archive on INVOICED**: When a job card's status transitions to `INVOICED` (via `PUT /:id` or `PATCH /:id/status`), the server automatically sets `archived = 1` and stamps `invoicedDate` with the current timestamp — on **both** routes the status write and the archive write run inside one `db.transaction`, so a failure between them can't leave a job reading INVOICED while still in the open list. Only management can set status to INVOICED. **Invoicing is an update-only transition**: a job is never *created* as INVOICED — the create route (`POST /`) rejects a `status` of `INVOICED` with 400, because only the update/status paths run the auto-archive + missing-files check, so allowing it at creation would strand a job in the invoiced-but-still-open limbo the status-lock exists to prevent. The status picker on the job screen mirrors this (INVOICED is offered only when editing an existing job, never while creating one). There is no manual archive endpoint; unarchive (`POST /:id/unarchive`, management) is the only way to reverse it. **An archived (invoiced/filed-away) job is closed to every write, not just status**: one middleware, `closedJobGuard` (`server/src/middleware/closedJob.js`), is mounted once ahead of every `/api/jobcards/:id` route (`app.use('/api/jobcards/:id', authenticate, closedJobGuard)` in `index.js`) rather than each route pasting in its own check, so a route added later is closed by default too. It reads the job by id and, when `archived === 1`, refuses any non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS request with 409 `{ error: 'This job is invoiced and closed. Unarchive it to make changes.', code: 'JOB_CLOSED' }` **before any write** — parts, comments, files, pricing, assignees, the job's own fields and its status are all included; there is no field left editable on a closed job any more. A short allow-list (one named constant in that file, with a one-line reason per entry) is let through anyway: `POST /:id/unarchive` (the way out of the lock), `DELETE /:id` (deleting the job itself, admin-only in its own route), `POST /:id/time-entries/:entryId/stop` (stopping a running timer always works), `POST /:id/print` / `POST /:id/packet` (building the job card preview and the combined PDF — sent as POST but they only read the job's current data, so a closed job's paperwork can still be viewed, printed and saved), and `POST /:id/printed` / `POST /:id/saved` (recording that paperwork was printed/saved, which doesn't change the job). The lock keys off the `archived` flag alone (invoicing always files a job away; unarchive always clears it). **Unarchive clears `INVOICED` and lets the logged work decide the status**: the `unarchive` query sets `OPEN` (never a back-in-the-list-but-still-INVOICED contradiction), then `syncStatusToWork` runs in the same transaction, so a job whose work is all counted comes back Done, one with some work In Progress, and one with none stays Open. The resulting status is recorded in the unarchive history entry alongside the `archived`/`invoicedDate` changes.

**One shared invoicing step for both routes**: `PUT /jobcards/:id` and `PATCH /jobcards/:id/status` are the only two routes that can move a job to `INVOICED`, and both run the exact same checks, in the same order, before any write, via one pair of functions in `jobcard-helpers.js` — `checkInvoicing(existing, newStatus, confirmMissingAttachments)` runs the two checkpoints below and returns either a `refusal` (a `{ status, body }` the caller sends back as-is) or `{ shouldArchive, invoicedDate }`; `applyInvoicingArchive(shouldArchive, invoicedDate, userId, jobcardId)` is called from inside the caller's own write transaction — it writes the archive row and returns the `{ archived, invoicedDate }` history-change entries for the caller to fold into its own `changes` object.

**Hard running-timer checkpoint**: `checkInvoicing` refuses **before any write**, and before the soft attachment checkpoint below, when any time entry on the job is still running (`end_time IS NULL`) — 409 `{ error: 'A timer is still running on this job. Stop it before marking the job invoiced.' }`. Unlike the missing-attachments checkpoint this is a hard block with no confirm-anyway body flag: a running timer can't be confirmed away, since invoicing archives the job and an archived job's time can no longer be changed (see `docs/notes/time-and-costing.md`) — stopping it after the fact wouldn't be possible. The same hard refusal covers a **just-stopped block whose worker is still filling in the stop-timer form**: rather than guessing this from a blank description and a timing window (both of which a hand-added block could trip for innocent reasons), the block carries an explicit `awaiting_details` flag — set to 1 by the stop-timer route the moment it stops a block, and cleared to 0 only by the worker's own stop-timer form save (the form sends `detailsConfirmed: true`, which nothing else sends) or by resuming the block (clearing its finish time reopens it, so there's no pending form left to wait on). A manager editing the block's other fields — or the separate manual time-entry form — leaves the flag exactly as it was, so a manager's edit can no longer end the wait mid-form; a hand-added block never carries it, since only the stop route sets it. This is computed by the route (`PUT /:id/time-entries/:entryId`) and passed into `timeEntryQueries.update` as a parameter, not hard-coded in the query. A block on the job still marked `awaiting_details` and stopped — or, for a clock that stopped itself, answered (`finish_confirmed_at`) — within the last 30 minutes refuses invoicing with 409 `'Someone has just stopped a timer on this job and is still filling in their pieces. Try again once they have saved it.'` — otherwise invoicing files the job away mid-form and the form's save is refused, losing the pieces, scrap and inspection answers. The 30-minute window means a form someone walked away from never blocks the job for good. Both checks live in one helper, `invoiceBlockedByTime` (`utils/timeEntryHelpers.js`), called from `checkInvoicing`.

**Hard unconfirmed-clock checkpoint**: checked right after the running-timer one (`invoiceBlockedByTime`), also before any write and with no confirm-anyway flag: any time entry on the job still flagged `finish_unconfirmed` (a clock that stopped itself and whose worker has not said when they really finished) → 409 `{ error: '<Name> has not confirmed when their clock on this job finished. Ask them to sign in and answer, or correct the time yourself.' }`, naming the first such worker. A management save of that row settles it. See `docs/notes/time-and-costing.md`.

**Soft close-out checkpoint**: When invoicing (which also archives) and any attachment gaps exist, `checkInvoicing` returns a refusal the caller sends as 409 `{ error: 'MISSING_ATTACHMENTS', attachmentWarnings }` **before any write**. The client shows an "Invoice anyway?" confirm and resends with `confirmMissingAttachments: true` in the body to bypass the check. **When the job declared files but the job-folders location can't be reached** (drive or network share offline), nothing is known about the files, so the checkpoint still stops before any write — 409 `{ error: 'FILES_UNREACHABLE', attachmentWarnings }` with `attachmentWarnings.filesUnreachable: true` — and `confirmInvoiceAnyway` asks "the job's files couldn't be checked … invoice anyway?" instead of listing gaps; the same `confirmMissingAttachments: true` resend bypasses it. An unchecked job is never invoiced (and archived) silently. This is a soft nudge, not a hard block. Both routes always read the job's current, already-saved items for this check (parts are never part of either invoicing route's own body — see "Assignees" below) — `computeAttachmentWarnings` takes only `(jobcardId, items)`; the "no permanent id yet" skip inside it is dead-in-practice defensive code, not a caller-selectable option (the flag that used to select it was removed).

**Second soft close-out checkpoint: unanswered Critical sign-offs.** Right after the missing-attachments checkpoint, `checkInvoicing` also checks for finished runs that needed the Critical sign-off (`time_entries.critical_at_finish = 1` — decided per run, at the moment it finished; see `docs/notes/files-and-qa.md`) but are still missing one of the four inspection answers (`timeEntryQueries.getMissingInspectionByJobcard`). If any, and the caller hasn't already confirmed, it refuses 409 `{ error: 'MISSING_INSPECTION', inspectionWarnings: [{ id, workerName, startTime, endTime, itemNumber }] }` — a warning, not a hard block, since only management can invoice anyway. The client's `confirmMissingAttachments` gets a sibling body flag, `confirmMissingInspection`, read the same way in both status routes; the job screen and the job list's status badge both handle either 409 in turn through the shared `changeJobStatus.js` (attachments first, then sign-off), each confirmed flag staying set on the resend so answering both questions sends both flags true. Invoicing anyway folds `inspectionSignOff: { from: '<N> run(s) unanswered', to: 'invoiced anyway' }` into the same trail entry as the archive (`applyInvoicingArchive`). The job screen marks each such run "Sign-off missing" on its logged-work list, independent of whether it's actually invoiced.

**Both places that can set `INVOICED` from the client ask the exact same questions, worded once.** The job screen's status control (`JobIdentityStrip.jsx`) and the job list's status badge (`JobCardList.jsx`'s `handleQuickStatusChange`) both call `confirmMarkInvoiced` ("Mark as Invoiced" — the job screen alone passes it a freshly-fetched total and whether costing was just saved, since only it has costing access), `confirmInvoiceAnyway` ("Invoice anyway?", for the missing-attachments case above), and `confirmInvoiceWithoutSignOff` ("Inspection sign-off missing", for the unanswered-sign-off case above) from `jobcard/jobCardPrompts.jsx`, rather than each screen keeping its own copy of the wording.

**The client has one rule for "is this job closed?"**: `isJobClosed(job)` in `client/src/utils/jobLock.js` reads the same `archived` flag the server's `closedJobGuard` keys on, and nothing in the client tests `status === 'INVOICED'` or the job list's "Show Archived" view toggle to decide whether a job can still be changed any more — both used to be used as proxies and could disagree with the row actually being closed (a manager viewing a closed job through search, or a stale `status` field, isn't necessarily archived, and the toggle says nothing about any one row on screen). The job screen's loaded job carries `archived` through into its form state (`mappers.js`'s `getDefaultFormData`, `useJobCardForm.js`'s `setFormDataFromJobCard`) — left out of the unsaved-edits snapshot the same way `status` is, since it's server-driven, never typed. On a closed job, `JobCardModal.jsx` shows one line at the top ("This job is invoiced and closed. Unarchive it to make changes.") and wraps the editable part of the Details tab's management view (fields, parts, workers — the comments lock themselves and stay outside, so their Retry still works) and of the Costing tab (the sheet body — `CostingTab`'s `locked` prop; its header's "what this job used" toggle and the load-failure Try again stay outside) each in a plain `<fieldset disabled>` (`.jc-lock-fieldset` in `JobCardModal.css` strips its default box so it doesn't disturb the layout) — this refuses interaction with every input, select, textarea and button inside it, for every role, without threading a lock prop through each one; the worker view is already fully read-only regardless. The per-item file-attach button and the timer Start/Stop buttons are hidden outright rather than left disabled, since a closed job can never have a timer running against it (invoicing is refused while one is) — there's nothing left to stop. **A write that reaches the server anyway** (the job was invoiced and archived from another PC while this screen still had it open) comes back with the 409/`JOB_CLOSED` shape above; the save queue (`useSaveQueue.js`, covering every field/part/worker write), the status control (`JobIdentityStrip.jsx`), comments (`useJobNotes.js`), manual time entries (`useTimeEntries.js`), the pricing sheet (`useCostingSave.js`, which also drops its unstored figures), timer start and the stop form's save/resume on this job (`useTimer.js` — which also closes the stop form when its save or resume is refused because the job was closed or the block deleted, since that form has no Escape and neither button could ever work again), and file uploads, re-tags and deletes (`useJobFiles.js`, via `JobPaperworkHub.jsx`'s `onJobClosed`) all recognise it (`jobLock.js`'s `isJobClosedError`) and call one shared handler (`JobCardModal.jsx`'s `handleJobClosedWrite`) instead of their ordinary failure toast — it shows the same sentence with a stable id and reloads the job, so the screen catches up and goes read-only. Timer stop itself is allow-listed through the lock, so it never meets this refusal; the "stop & switch" start is still not wired (it is safely refused server-side with its own error). The status control's own invoicing is the one close that comes from this screen rather than elsewhere: `changeJobStatus.js` hands the status reply to its caller, and `JobIdentityStrip.jsx` reloads the job when that reply says the job is archived, so the screen locks at once. The header strip (priority, description, due date, status) sits outside the lock fieldsets, so it checks `isJobClosed` itself and shows plain text on a closed job. Inside the Details lock, a finished run's view-only "Inspection" expander is still disabled on a closed job (it sits inside the parts list, which is locked as one piece).

## Deleting a job

**Soft delete checkpoint**: `DELETE /jobcards/:id` (admin) never deletes on the first request — because deleting is permanent and the job number is never reused, the server always returns 409 `{ error: 'CONFIRM_DELETE', workWarning }` **before any write** unless the body carries `confirmDelete: true`. `workWarning` is `null` when the job has no recorded work (client shows a plain "are you sure"); when any time has been logged or a timer is running (both cascade away on delete) it carries `{ hasActive, activeWorkers, loggedHours, pastWorkers }` so the confirm can name who/what is being erased. The confirmation lives entirely in this one 409 round-trip — there is no separate client-side pre-confirm — so the admin only ever sees a single dialog. Resending with `confirmDelete: true` bypasses the gate. Mirrors the missing-attachments checkpoint.

## Comments (notes)

Notes endpoints: `GET /jobcards/:id/notes` (authenticated — **newest first**, `created_at DESC` with `rowid` as tie-break), `POST /jobcards/:id/notes` (authenticated), `DELETE /jobcards/:id/notes/:noteId` (management), `PUT /jobcards/:id/notes/read` (authenticated, body `{ seenUpTo }`; see unread below). The **job list response also carries each job's newest comment** as `latestNote` (`{ text, userName, createdAt }`, or `null`) — fetched for all listed jobs in one pass by `getLatestNotesForJobcards` (`db/queries/operations.js`, a `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY jobcard_id ORDER BY created_at DESC, rowid DESC)` pick, i.e. **the same ordering the thread uses**, so the column can never show a different comment than the top of the thread when two share a timestamp; it returns raw rows and the route converts to camelCase at the boundary) and rendered as the **Latest Comment** column sitting between Status and Priority in the job list (full text floats on hover with author + time). Adding or deleting a comment in the job screen hands the newest remaining comment back to the list via `onNotesChange`, which **patches that one row in place** (never a whole-list re-fetch). It comes straight from the write's own reply — the new comment from the add, `latestNote` (same ordering as the thread) from the delete — so the row updates even if the window closed meanwhile, and the thread is re-read only while the window is still open. The column ids `latestNote` and `print` must each exist in **both** `DEFAULT_COLUMN_ORDER` (`JobCardList.constants.js`) and its server mirror `JOBCARD_COLUMN_IDS` (`middleware/validation.js`) — the server validates saved column order/visibility against that list, so a column missing there breaks reordering for everyone. The **Print** column reads `printedAt` straight off each job in the list response (stamped by the print-confirmation route once a packet carrying the job card has actually reached a viewer — see `docs/notes/files-and-qa.md`) and sorts via a getter in `useJobCardSort.js`, the same pattern every sortable column follows. `mergeColumnOrder` folds a newly-added column into a user's saved order at its default position and always keeps `actions` last. The Excel export re-reverses the thread so its Notes cell still reads oldest-first.

**Comments live in their own window, not in the Details tab.** On an existing job, every role and every tab, a round chat bubble (with a red count of *new* comments, nothing when there are none) floats just outside the job window's top-left edge. Pressing it slides a 360px comments window open to the left of the job (`JobCommentsPanel.jsx`, handed to `BottomSheet` as its `aside`): the job window keeps its size and the comments hang outside its left edge. To make room the pair slides right just far enough for the comments to fit in the left margin (never pushing the job off the right of the screen); when the screen is too narrow for both, the comments overlap the job's left edge instead. The slide is a margin, not a transform, because a transform would become the anchor for every fixed-position pop-up inside the job window. It reads like a chat: oldest at the top, the signed-in person's own comments on the right in the accent colour, everyone else's on the left with initials and name, day separators, and comments by one person within five minutes grouped. Enter sends, Shift+Enter is a new line. Escape pressed inside the comments window closes only that window (it marks the key handled, so the job window's own Escape stands down); the row holding both windows is the job window's Tab trap, so focus can move between them. Whether the window is open is decided afresh each time the job is opened (see unread below); nothing is remembered in the browser. Deleting a comment is management-only (a trash icon shown on hover, with the usual confirm). On an invoiced (closed) job the typing box and delete are replaced by a line saying to unarchive first. An unposted comment still counts as unsaved work when the job is closed — and so does one still sending (its text has already left the box): closing waits for it alongside the job's own saves, up to the same few seconds; a failed send puts the draft back and the usual unposted-comment question follows, one still on its way after the limit is named as "Your comment is still being sent", and a refresh while it sends gets the browser's leave-page question.

**Unread comments, per person.** A comment is *unread* for a person when someone else wrote it and it is newer than the moment that person last saw the job's comments. Their own comments are never unread. It is stored on the server per person per job (table `job_note_reads`: `user_id`, `jobcard_id`, `seen_up_to` = the `created_at` of the newest comment seen; cascades with the job) because workers share PCs. A person's effective "seen up to" is the greatest of their own row, the launch baseline (setting `comments_read_from`, stamped once with the current moment by a startup conversion in `legacyMigrations.js` only when absent, so comments that existed before the feature don't all arrive as unread; a restored older backup gets it stamped by the same conversion pass) and their account's `created_at` (a new worker inherits no backlog). That rule is written once, as `SEEN_UP_TO_SQL` in `db/queries/operations.js`, and used by both the single-job value and the list count. `GET /jobcards/:id` carries `commentsSeenUpTo` for the signed-in person; the job list carries `unreadNotes` per job (one query for all listed ids, `getUnreadNoteCountsForJobcards`). `PUT /jobcards/:id/notes/read` takes `{ seenUpTo }` (any ISO-8601 moment, rewritten to the stored milliseconds-and-Z shape before anything compares it as text), clamps it to the newest comment actually on the job, only ever moves the mark forward, and returns `{ commentsSeenUpTo, unreadNotes }` (the person's unread count for that job afterwards, from the same counting as the list); the effective "seen up to" falls back to the 1970 moment when none of the three exist, never an empty string; it is allowed on a closed job (listed in `ALLOWED_ON_CLOSED_JOB`) and writes no trail entry. On screen: once both the job and the first read of the thread have arrived, the comments window opens by itself if anything is unread and stays closed otherwise — decided once per opening (each opening is a fresh job window, so the decision is made on that opening's own thread and read mark, never on the previous one's), never again, and without moving focus off the job (focus moves only when the person presses the bubble or the close button). Whenever the window is open and the newest comment is newer than the mark (including the person's own just-posted comment), the screen sends the read call and takes the reply as the new mark; a failure is silent and retried the next time the window is opened, never in a loop. Pressing the bubble re-reads the thread first, so a comment posted from another PC shows up and is counted as read. A thin "New" line sits above the first comment that was unread when the job was opened (worked out once per opening, kept until the job closes). The header line reads "J-2417, 5 comments, 2 new". In the job list, a job with unread comments shows a small accent dot before its Latest Comment and the text in bold, titled "2 new comments"; reading the thread sets that row to the returned count in place (`onCommentsRead`), and it still does when the window was closed before the reply arrived, because the call names its job; the finish-question's own job window passes it too (it reloads the list), the search page doesn't because its results carry no unread mark.

**Mentions.** A comment can @mention staff. `POST /jobcards/:id/notes` takes an optional `mentionUserIds` (an array of at most 20 non-empty strings; anything else is a 400). The route drops repeats and the writer's own id (mentioning yourself is ignored silently); every other id must be an existing **active** person, or the whole post is refused with a 400 whose `fields` marks the text box (the validator's own refusals — too many ids, not a list, bad entries — are reported under `text` as well, via `FIELD_ALIASES` in `validation.js`, so every mention refusal marks the same box) — the comment box shows it under itself while the job window is up, and it is a pop-up naming the job only if the window has closed. An archived person gets "<Name> can no longer be mentioned — their account is archived." with `code: 'MENTION_INACTIVE'`, which the client branches on; an id that names nobody at all (unknown, or with stray spaces) is a garbled request and gets the validator's "Couldn’t tell who was asked — pick them again from the @ list." with no code. Each mention is its own `job_note_mentions` row (`note_id`, `jobcard_id`, `user_id`, `mentioned_name` = their name or username as it reads after the @, `created_at` = the comment's, `answered_at`); the 201 reply carries `mentions: [{ userId, name }]`, and the comment's trail entry carries a `mentioned` field (`from: null`, `to: 'Name One, Name Two'`). `GET /jobcards/:id/notes` gives every comment a `mentions` array (empty when none), from one extra read for the whole job. **The answer rule:** a mention is *open* until the mentioned person posts any comment on that same job after it; that one comment answers **all** their open mentions on the job, in the same transaction as the post. `GET /jobcards/open-mentions` (any role, registered ahead of the `/:id` routes in `jobcard-notes.js`; a GET is never stopped by the closed-job lock) returns the caller's open mentions grouped per job, oldest waiting first: `{ jobcardId, jobNumber, description, count, firstNoteId, oldestAt, firstText, firstByName }` (the `first*` fields describe the oldest open mention's comment — the one the row opens at, so what the row shows, its time and where it lands all agree). `GET /auth/me` carries `openMentions: { count, signature }` (`signature` is built from one cheap summary of what is waiting — how many, the newest mention's time and the sorted ids of the visible jobs holding them — so a mention added or answered, or a job archived or unarchived (the id list changes, so even one archived while another is unarchived), shows without a second request; an ordinary edit to one of those jobs does not change it; `null` if that read failed). **Open mentions on invoiced (archived) jobs are left out of the list and the count** — nothing can be posted there to answer them — and they return if the job is unarchived. Backups before data version 9 restore the table empty. **On screen: the "Needs your attention" window.** `context/FinishQuestionProvider.jsx` (which composes the clock question and the mentions into the one window; the mentions side — list, row-opened job, re-read, held flag — is `hooks/useMentionAttention.js`) reads the list at sign-in, whenever the `/auth/me` poll reports a new `openMentions.signature` (`AuthContext` writes it into the small store in `context/openMentionsMarker.js`, which `FinishQuestionProvider` watches; `hooks/useOpenMentions.js` does the read, newest read wins, a failed read keeps the old list and forgets the marker, so the next poll that gets through reads again even when nothing changed — the retry rides the poll, never a loop of its own) and after a job opened from a row closes. The mentions are the "Questions for you" section of `common/AttentionDialog.jsx` (the same blocking window that carries the forgotten-clock question): an instruction line ("Open each one and reply — any reply counts. This closes once they're all answered."), then one button row per job — job number, " — description" in lighter text, then "<name>: “<comment>”" for the oldest open question, "asked <time>" (time if today, else short date), "N questions" when more than one, and an arrow as the open cue. An @name counts only as a whole word: a person answers to their full display name and, when it has more than one word, to its first word too ("@Sam" for "Sam Smith"). The text after the @ must be that name (capitals ignored), followed by the end or something that is not a letter or digit, and the longest name wins ("@Jo Bloggs" never also mentions Jo; "@Joanne" never highlights "@Jo"). A matched name belongs to the people whose FULL name it is; only if there are none, to the people whose first name it is. One person: them. Several: the one picked from the @ list, else the name is *unclear* (never silently nobody). The one rule, and the one lookup built from the staff list (lower-cased name -> `{ display, full, first }`), is `components/jobcard/mentionNames.js`, used for who a sent comment mentions, for the live "Will ask" line and for highlighting (a shown comment is searched against the same lookup built (`buildNameLookup`) from the whole staff list plus every person the thread's comments mention (`mentionedPeople`) — one lookup per thread, so someone since archived still reads whole; which names count as stored mentions is `storedMentionsByName`, also in `mentionNames.js`, not a second copy in the panel; sending still uses the active staff only — longest name first, and only a name that is one of its stored mentions is highlighted — so with Sam Smith stored, "@Sam Jones" is read as the whole name Sam Jones and nothing is highlighted; a first word like "@Sam" is highlighted as a stored person only when sending would have read it as them — nobody's whole name is "Sam" and, the writer aside, they are the only Sam in that same name set — so an unclear "@Sam" sent with "Send without asking them" is never coloured as the Sam who was mentioned by full name). **The writer is never a match for an @name**: the lookup is built from the whole staff list, the writer included, so where a name ends is read the same for everyone ("@Sam Jones" written by Sam Jones is that whole name, never "@Sam" plus a surname that would ask Sam Smith), and the writer is then left out of who it means (`resolveMentions`, the same rule as the @ list): an @name that only fits the writer asks nobody, and a first name shared with the writer is not "which one?". The writer's name counts as known for the "Nobody here is called…" check, so a self-mention posts quietly with no confirm. Who a comment mentions is worked out from its finished text against the active staff list when it is sent, so a name typed out by hand counts the same as one picked from the @ list. **Picks** (people chosen from the @ list) only settle a name that several people share; a pick counts only while that name is still in the text, and all picks are forgotten whenever the box becomes empty by any route (typing, deleting, sending — one place, the setter the panel uses). **Nothing is sent without the writer knowing who will be asked**: under the box, whenever the draft mentions anyone, the hint reads "Will ask: Jo Bloggs, Sam Smith" (full names, the writer left out; an unclear name shows as "Chris (which one?)"), worked out live by the same rule as sending, so a typo like "@Jo Blogs" visibly asks Jo. **An @word that names nobody, or a shared name with no pick, is never sent silently**: before posting, the staff list is fetched again (the window's copy may be empty or stale) — only when some such word has not already been checked against a fresh list in this window — and, if a word still matches nobody (`findUnmatchedMentions`), the writer is asked "Nobody here is called “Bob”, so nobody will be asked. Send anyway?" (Send anyway / Keep editing); a name with several people and no pick is asked as 'There is more than one person called “Chris” — pick the one you mean from the @ list. Send without asking them?' (Send without asking them / Keep editing); both in one comment is one confirm covering both. Only a word starting with a letter counts as a tried name ("@3pm", "@12" are ignored). A comment naming more than 20 people is stopped before sending and the comment box says "A comment can ask at most 20 people." (`MAX_MENTIONS`, `server/src/shared/mentions.js`, also the route's limit). **Sending is chat-style** (a send or delete moves through one stage in `useJobNotes.js` — idle, checking, sending or deleting, back to idle in a single `finally`; anything but idle gates Send, Enter and the delete buttons, "sending" alone is what close treats as a comment still on its way, and the stage is let go before the thread is re-read; the thread's own "loading" flag only means the thread is being read). **The checks can be cancelled**: after each wait in them (the fresh staff list, the "Send anyway?" question) the send carries on only if the job window is still up and the box still holds exactly the checked text; if the person closed the job meanwhile (and agreed to lose the unposted comment) or changed the text, it stops quietly and posts nothing. Deleting a comment is refused (with the "Still sending a comment" pop-up) before its "Delete?" question when a send is busy. While the checks run the box is read-only (so the text checked is the text sent), the @ list stays shut and picks are ignored; once they pass the sent text leaves the box and the picks are cleared at once, before the save. If the save fails the draft comes back (in front of anything typed meanwhile, separated by a new line) with its picks, and the refusal marks the box as before. Only a refusal coded `MENTION_INACTIVE` (a person archived meanwhile) reads the staff list again so they drop off the @ list; other failures do not. Two staff whose names differ only by capitals are told apart by the person picked from the list. **While the @ list is open, Enter never sends**: with a name highlighted it takes it; with nothing highlighted it closes the list (as Escape does) and the next Enter sends — a half-typed "@Jo" can't go out by accident (a worker can't delete their own comment). With no mention in the draft the hint under the box reads "Type @ to ask someone · Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line". Posting any comment on a job, from any job window, takes that job's row off the list at once (the post answered it) and then reads the list again only when there is something to settle: a row was showing for that job, or a read is already on its way (it may carry a question for that job that the post has just answered, and only a newer read can throw it away). Otherwise the next `/auth/me` poll covers it — a question asked since the last read and then answered by this post changes the signature, which brings its own read. Sign-in makes one read: the login sets the marker before the person, so the list is read once the person is known, with the marker already there. Only the newest read is ever applied, so a read already on its way — possibly made before the reply was saved — is thrown away instead of bringing the answered row back. Pressing a row opens that job in the provider's own job window with its comments open, scrolled to the oldest open mention, cursor in the reply box; the attention window is hidden meanwhile and, on close, the list is read again — the row is gone if the person replied, still there if not. Because closing waits for a reply still sending (see above), that read leaves only after the reply has saved. Everyone gets it, admins included. **It waits until no other window is open** (the shared modal stack, `common/modalStack.js`, says so): a person typing on a job screen is not interrupted and gets it the moment they close that window, while someone with nothing open gets it straight away; once the mentions are up they stay up (that holds for the mentions section itself — a clock question opening over a job screen never lets the rows in behind it), and they are hidden while a stop form is showing, while a check for owed stop forms is still running (at sign-in, after the clock is answered, after a stop form closes — if the mentions are already up they stay up, greyed out, until the check ends, so the window never closes and reopens), and after a job opened from a row closes until the list has been read again (a read overtaken by a newer one only counts as done once the newest has landed), so an answered row never flashes back. **The clock section is the exception**: a flagged clock shows over everything, as before, and while it shows every mention row is greyed out with "Answer your clock first." (while only the owed-stop-form check holds them, the note reads "One moment…"). What the window shows — clock, greyed or pressable rows, the reason — is decided in one place, `decideAttention` in `context/attentionDue.js`; nothing else re-derives it. **The cursor is never put on Sign out**: when the content changes, focus already on an answer control stays; otherwise it goes to the first pressable control in the sections, or to the window itself if none is pressable yet, and moves to the first row the moment the rows become pressable. The order when several are owed: the clock question, then owed stop forms, then mentions. The only way out besides answering is the **Sign out** button in the footer (no close button, Escape does nothing; when a screen behind holds unsaved work, e.g. a new job being typed, it first asks "Sign out? You have an unsaved job card. Signing out now will lose it." with Sign out / Stay signed in); the window goes away by itself once nothing is left.

## Assignees

**A worker can't be taken off a job while their clock is running on it** — by themselves or by the office (409), or the job would show nobody on it while time is being logged. Stop the clock first.

Assignee endpoints: `PUT /jobcards/:id` no longer takes `assigneeIds` at all — the branch that reconciled a whole list was stripped in Stage 4b of `tasks/instant-save-job-card.md` once nothing sent it any more (the job screen writes one worker at a time, and `buildJobcardPayload` only puts `assigneeIds` in the **create** payload). `POST /jobcards/:id/assignees/self` (authenticated, idempotent self-assign — uses `req.user.userId`, body ignored), `DELETE /jobcards/:id/assignees/self` (authenticated, idempotent self-unassign). Self routes log history with action `self_assign` / `self_unassign`. `PUT /jobcards/:id/assignees/:userId` and `DELETE /jobcards/:id/assignees/:userId` (both management, idempotent, 404 if the user doesn't exist) put or take off **one** worker without touching anyone else's row — the instant-save equivalent of the self routes, for the person ticking names on someone else's behalf. History action `assign` / `unassign`; both keep the same `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE` swallow the self routes use, since a timer auto-assigning the same worker can race the same insert. These are what the job screen's people tiles now call on every tap. **All four routes are refused on an archived (invoiced) job** by `closedJobGuard` (see "Invoicing and archiving" above) before the route itself ever runs, with `409 { error: 'This job is invoiced and closed. Unarchive it to make changes.', code: 'JOB_CLOSED' }`; the job list's Assigned To column and the job screen's people controls go read-only on such a job the same way the status badge already does, so the refusal is normally never hit from the screen.

Item endpoints, same instant-save batch (`server/src/routes/jobcard-items.js`, management, wired into the job screen's parts list via `useInstantItems.js`): `POST /jobcards/:id/items` adds one part (closed by `closedJobGuard` like every other write on an archived job — see "Invoicing and archiving" above); `PATCH /jobcards/:id/items/:itemId` changes one part — absent fields are unchanged, the body is merged over the stored row before validating, and the part never moves position; `DELETE /jobcards/:id/items/:itemId` removes one part (blocked if time is logged against it, or if it's the job's last remaining line). All three run the same seven item validators the create route (`POST /jobcards`) uses, grandfathering values already saved elsewhere on the job, and each names the part in its error message by description rather than position (a one-element validation batch can't report a meaningful array index) — `PUT /jobcards/:id` no longer takes `items` either, so these are now the *only* way an existing job's parts change. **A part's `item_number` is a sort order the server owns, not its identity — its permanent `item:` id is.** A new part gets `MAX(item_number) + 1` for the job, computed inside the same transaction as its insert, so it can never collide with a number picked at the same moment or repeat a gap. **Nothing renumbers on delete** — gaps are expected and fine; the number shown on screen is the part's `position`, a display-only field the **server** states on every part it returns — its 1-based index in that job's parts ordered by `item_number` ascending. A screen never counts this for itself any more (it used to, per-screen, before this field existed) and never sends `position` anywhere or writes it onto a row — identity is always the permanent `item:` id. A one-time startup conversion (`cleanUpDuplicateItemNumbering` in `db/legacyMigrations.js`) folds any job whose numbers still carry **duplicates** from before this change onto a clean 1..n ordering; gaps are left exactly as they are, since closing them on every boot is the very instability this change removed. It runs on every boot and is a no-op once a job has no duplicates. History folds into the job's `update` action, keyed by the part's description (`part "X" added` / `part "X"` / `part "X" removed`) rather than its number, since a part's number is no longer stable enough to identify it across edits; a no-op edit (summary unchanged) writes no history row. Each of the three routes returns the job's full, freshly-recomputed part list (`items`, each carrying its own `position`) and `attachmentWarnings` alongside its own result, the same way the whole-job save already does, so a screen acting on the reply never has to separately re-fetch either.

`PUT /jobcards/:id` itself, after Stage 4b, only ever touches the job's own single-value fields (status, priority, due date, description, PO/quote/previous-job references, quality level, repeat job) plus the invoice-time archive. It takes no `items` and no `assigneeIds` — sending either is simply ignored (an unrecognised body key, same as any other), and the delete-guard against removing a line with logged time now lives solely in `jobcard-items.js`'s own `DELETE` route.

**A previous-job reference only exists on a repeat job.** `POST /jobcards` and `PUT /jobcards/:id` store `repeat_job_reference` as null whenever the job ends up not being a repeat job (the PUT records the clearing in the trail), and a startup conversion clears any reference left on a non-repeat job. On screen, unticking Repeat Job clears the reference box along with the tick — it used to only hide it, so the old reference kept printing, exporting and matching searches. **A reference sent for a job that isn't (and this write isn't making) a repeat job is refused, not silently cleared**: `PUT /jobcards/:id` only takes the silent-clear path above when the same write also ends the job's repeat-job status (unticking it now, or it already wasn't one and nothing non-empty was sent) — a non-empty reference arriving any other way (the previous-job reference box's own instant-save write, sent alone, on a screen that still shows Repeat Job ticked after another PC unticked it) gets 400 `{ error, fields: [{ field: 'repeatJobReference', message: 'This job is no longer a repeat job — tick Repeat Job first.' }] }` instead, so the box marks itself rather than reading "Saved" with nothing stored.

## Intended, not findings

Each of these was decided (2026-10-14); a review or bug hunt does not raise it.

- **Marking comments as read writes no trail entry.** `PUT /jobcards/:id/notes/read` is not an edit of the job and would add an entry every time the comments window opened.

- **No shared "write a change and its trail entry" helper.** Every route writes its change and its `recordHistory` entry inside its own explicit `db.transaction`. A wrapper was considered and rejected: it cannot know which other steps (a sign-out, a status follow-up) belong inside, which is the mistake it would be meant to prevent.
- **The first trail entry of a job words its workers like every later one** (`assigneeNames`, `from: 'none'`), read back from the rows the create just wrote.
- **Answering a mention writes no trail entry.** It is a side effect of the person's own comment, which already has its entry.
- **A mention stays answered even if the answering comment is later deleted.** The answer is the fact that the person replied; the deletion does not reopen it.
- **Deleting the comment that asked a question drops the question with it, silently.** Once the comment is gone nobody is asking anything, so there is nothing left to answer or flag; the deletion's own trail entry is enough.
- **The @name in an old comment is not rewritten when the person is renamed.** The comment keeps what was typed, as every comment's author name used to before the rename sync.
- **An archived (deactivated) person's open mentions are left as they are** and reappear if the account is reactivated.
- **Open mentions on invoiced/archived jobs are hidden, not answered.** They are not counted or listed; unarchiving the job brings them back.
- **The mentions section waits only for open windows.** A page with its own unsaved form (not a window) can be covered by it; what was typed stays underneath.
- **A mention arriving while the person is in that same job's comments and replies there never shows a row.** The reply answers it before the list is read again.

Mentions — decided with the owner (2026-10-15); a review or bug hunt does not raise these either:

- **Only the person's own reply clears a mention.** Nobody — not the office, not an admin — can mark it dealt with for them; a question answered in person still gets a typed reply ("sorted in person").
- **No ready-made replies.** No quick-reply buttons or suggested answers: the person types what they mean, and any comment they send counts.
- **Anyone active can be mentioned**, not only the people on the job.
- **Admins get the window too.** Same rule for every role.
- **Mentions are live, not sign-in only.** The list appears while signed in and keeps itself up to date, because admins are never signed out for inactivity and would otherwise not hear about a question for days.
- **Blocking, with Sign out as the only exit.** Someone with several questions waiting replies to every one before carrying on; that is intended.
- **One window, clock first.** The forgotten-clock question and the mention rows share one window; the clock is always answered first (it affects pay and billing), mention rows stay greyed until it is.
- **Mentions wait for open windows; the clock does not.** Chosen over interrupting at once: a question never lands on someone mid-way through a job screen.
